subject: Decision Making
subcategory: Famous Decisions That Changed the World
title: Lincoln Frees the Enslaved
description: A short lesson to help you apply Lincoln Frees the Enslaved.

hook.text: Lincoln waited 18 months into the Civil War to issue the Emancipation Proclamation. The timing was a careful choice.

buildup.text: He needed a Union victory first. Freeing people from slavery during defeats would look like an act of desperation.

discovery.text: The Battle of Antietam gave him the win he needed. Five days later, he announced the Proclamation.

twist.text: The Proclamation only freed enslaved people in Confederate states, not border states. It was strategic, not idealistic.

climax.text: Lincoln timed his decision for maximum political impact. When you decide matters as much as what you decide.

punchline.text: Right decision, right moment. Timing turned strategy into history.

quiz.question: Why did Lincoln wait to issue the Emancipation Proclamation?
options: He needed a military victory first so it wouldn't seem desperate
